reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is to render text that remains legible against arbitrary backgrounds while maintaining a consistent visual style. This requires separating two distinct tasks: (1) a live, interactive preview using CSS transforms to adjust position, scale, and color, and (2) a final baked PNG that merges the text directly into the image pixels, eliminating dependency on external resources. Mathematically, the overlay is a composition of translation, rotation, and color mapping T(x) = R·(x - t) + c, where x is pixel coordinates, R is the font rasterizer, t is translation, and c is color. The bake operation then performs a pointwise blend B(x) = α·T(x) + (1-α)·I(x), where I is the background image and α is opacity. The key invariant is that B must reproduce exactly the CSS preview when α=0, ensuring consistency. Failure occurs when the stroke order is reversed (paint-order: stroke fill), causing the stroke to occlude the fill, or when font loading is not awaited, resulting in fallback system fonts. The method also generalizes to other typography styles by swapping the CSS rules, demonstrating a derived kernel pattern.
